lines: 7 committed files in js/ and css/ are source, not build output, and left out of the comparison:
js/dlhgshows-admin.js: named in templates/admin.php, and left as it is by the build
js/dlhgshows-main.js: named in templates/index.php, and left as it is by the build
css/admin.css: named in appinfo/routes.php, and left as it is by the build
css/main.css: named in templates/index.php, and left as it is by the build

The build reads what the source imports, so those files stay in the rebuilt tree. A file the app names in PHP, a template or info.xml, or in a script by its full path, is loaded by that name, and so is what it imports. Where no build writes other bytes under such a name, the file is a hand-written script, stylesheet or asset.
Neither the checkout nor the build has js/ or css/, so not a file could be compared.
--build=DIR names the directories this build writes, where they are not the ones above.
1 tracked file has uncommitted changes, and the rebuild used the working tree as it is, not the last commit.
So this says whether the output matches the source you are looking at, which is what a build would do. Against HEAD the answer can be another one.
npm install and npm run build succeed on the tracked files alone, twice, in 7.7 s.
Nothing else was in the tree, which is the state a fresh clone and CI build in, so a build that needs a leftover from an earlier one would have failed here.
